title: Rhythm versus melody information in music imagery
disposition_reason: Authenticated original metadata establishes no different-composition alternatives sharing declared tempo and meter in either stimulus version; no distinct excerpts share exact recorded full song duration. Equal windows cannot create the absent different-melody tempo overlap. The existing21-person music/score runtime remains a different target. No original-target neural grading is supported.

scientific_target.question: Within a verified tempo-,meter- and duration-matched OpenMIIR excerpt set, does imagery EEG reduce held-out identity loss beyond rhythm,cue and timing predictors?
scientific_target.known_answer: No numerical neural answer is instantiated for the intended matched-melody contrast. The exact source metadata establishes empty full-duration match support and only same-composition tempo/meter pairs; that is a design finding, not a measured neural target or an EEG failure.
scientific_target.answer_origin: Both original OpenMIIR stimulus workbooks and pinned author version semantics, complete twelve-stimulus roster per version, original song/lyric cue presentation, and independent exhaustive pair review. No EEG/audio waveform or participant inference was read.
scientific_target.case_unit: Proposed participant/repetition-held matched-excerpt comparison, not the 21-person score-guided bar case in the runtime declaration.
scientific_target.independent_unit: OpenMIIR participant, with excerpts/repetitions nested and dependence across matched stimuli disclosed.
scientific_target.inference_scope: The original proposed rhythm-versus-melody investigation is unsupported by source stimulus overlap. Within-version tempo/meter pairs are different recordings of the same composition; they do not identify a melody-specific contrast. Exact numeric equality is at recorded metadata precision, not proof of identical detailed or imagined rhythms. Equal-duration cropping is not an identified repair of missing cross-composition tempo overlap.
exclusions: Do not present 21-person music/score decoding as an OpenMIIR rhythm-versus-melody result.
Ordinary identity accuracy does not establish melody information beyond rhythm.
No pure imagery/causal mechanism, calibrated native performance or completed protected grading.
Do not count a negative source-design finding as a neural-understanding benchmark result.
Do not relabel same-composition vocal/instrumental rendition identity as a different-melody contrast.
Do not use rounded paper-table durations or mix stimulus versions to fabricate match support.

inputs: For the original question: verified no-concurrent-audio imagery EEG, fixed equal-length windows, train-only excerpt labels and declared tempo/meter/duration/cue covariates.

Any original matched contrast must have real source overlap. Both original versions have no different-composition tempo/meter alternatives; exact recorded full-duration matching has zero pairs. Fixed-length windows cannot restore different-melody tempo support.
forbidden_inputs: Query excerpt identity, audio/cue metadata that uniquely identifies the excerpt, duration-coded windows, held labels and post-hoc matched-set selection.

primary.rationale: The intended incremental-information endpoint cannot be graded on the verified original matched-melody support. The source audit is not a replacement neural metric. General excerpt identity or vocal/instrumental rendition questions require explicitly separate targets.

evaluation.failure_policy: Do not calculate the original melody-specific scientific endpoint: verified source metadata does not supply its required matched alternatives. If the complete visual song/lyric cue identity is admitted, target identity is deterministic by design; a positive conditional EEG-information claim cannot follow. This is not an observed classifier result.
